defects.claim: An action without `requires` gets a different deps bag from `trigger`/`begin`/`preview` than from its own bindings
defects.scenario: an action declares no `requires`, and its `run` reads `deps.selection`. When the palette or a menu fires it through `ActionsRegistry.trigger`, `depsFor` hands over the fixed legacy bag (selection, scene, history, view, activeTool, booleansAdapter), so it works. When its own key binding fires it, the dispatcher builds the bag with `createActionDeps(action, …)` (walk.ts:176), which reads `requires ?? []` and passes an empty bag. In dev that bag is the undeclared-read Proxy, so `deps.selection` throws; in prod it is `undefined`. The same split shows up in `begin` vs a gesture and in `registry.preview` vs `dropPreview`. The same action should get the same deps on every path. walk.ts's comment says the bag is "Shared with `ActionsRegistry.trigger`, including the dev undeclared-read guard", but the legacy branch is a plain object with no guard.
defects.cause: two dep-bag builders, one keeping a legacy fallback

defects.claim: A merged tuning form loses the added form's name when the action's own form has no name
defects.scenario: an action's own `params` form has `name: ''`, which `PrefGroup` defines as "no heading". A tuning adds a `form` named "Brush". `formWith` returns `{ ...form, ...a, … }`, so own's empty `name` overwrites "Brush". The last-operation panel then titles the run `schema.name || action.label`, which gives the action's label instead of "Brush". This contradicts formWith's own doc: "named for `own` where it names itself".
defects.cause: spread lets an empty name win

defects.claim: The last-operation wrapper seals history after an ongoing action's start instead of before, so an edit made in start coalesces with the gesture's later stops
defects.scenario: an ongoing action that declares `params` and whose handle has `replay`, and whose `start` writes its first edit straight to the history (no journal) with later moves coalescing into it. `invoker.start(ctx, opts)` runs first, then `watchEntry(stack)` calls `stack.seal()`, so the moves' edits can no longer coalesce into the entry `start` pushed: one gesture leaves two undo entries only because a history is present and the action declares `params`. The watch also never saw that first push, so the later coalesce or push marks it unclean and the operation is not kept either. The immediate path (`wrap`) seals before running; the ongoing path should seal before `start` too (the stack is already read before `start`).
defects.cause: seal ordered after start

defects.claim: An unparseable binding override warns again on every change to the actions tree
defects.scenario: A host passes `overrideBindings({ 'undo.key': 'Mod+Z' })`, a shortcut rather than a route.
defects.cause: warning not deduplicated across cache recomputes

defects.claim: withRoleMods widens a binding for a role whose old keys only an earlier role's widening admitted
defects.scenario: An action declares role A with keys `['shift']` and role B with keys `['alt']`. Its binding is written with mods `{ shift: 'optional' }`, so it admits A's key and not B's. A tuning moves A to `['alt']` and B to `['ctrl']`. The loop handles A first: A's old key `shift` is admitted, so `allow('alt')` adds `alt: 'optional'` to `mods`. Then it handles B. The check `was.every((k) => admitted(mods, k))` reads that same mutated `mods`, so B's old key `alt` now passes, and `ctrl` is widened as well. Ctrl-drags now reach a binding that was never written for role B. Reverse the role declaration order and `ctrl` is not widened, so the result depends on the order roles are declared in.
defects.cause: the admitted check reads mods being widened, not the spec's own mods

defects.claim: pushOwner's release removes the newest copy of a value pushed twice, reordering the stack
defects.scenario: One value is pushed twice onto the same owner stack, for example a module-constant `BindingOverrides` map or `ActionTuning` that two components pass to `overrideBindings` / `tune` on one node. Another holder's value sits between the two. The stack is `[T(first), U, T(second)]`. When the first holder releases, `lastIndexOf(value)` removes index 2, which is the second holder's slot, leaving `[T, U]`. U now beats T, although the T still registered was pushed after U and should win: "a later one beats an earlier one in the same scope". The doc promises that "the release takes out *its own* entry wherever it now sits", but with equal values it cannot find its own entry.
defects.cause: release identifies its entry by value, not by a per-push token

defects.claim: A grouped settings form's default change params use a dotted flat key while its values and the last operation are nested
defects.scenario: An `ActionSettings` whose schema has a group (leaf path `stroke.width`) and no `params` function. `read()` returns values nested as the groups nest, and menus and panels read them back with `prefValueAt(values, 'stroke.width')`. When that field changes, the default returns `{ 'stroke.width': v }`, a literal dotted key. The action is triggered with it, so an invoker reading `params.stroke?.width` (the nested shape that `read` and the last-operation keeper's `withValues` / `nestPrefValues` use) gets nothing, and the change is silently dropped. Only flat schemas work with the default.
defects.cause: default params not nested at the leaf path

defects.claim: A variant key can equal another action's id, so a saved menu entry resolves to the wrong action
defects.scenario: Action `align` with variant `left` and a separate action `align:left` both get key `align:left`; resolveMenu matches the exact action id first and runs the separate action
defects.cause: generated variant key not unique against action ids

defects.claim: handleWith's proxy breaks on a frozen handle, so reading a method throws a TypeError
defects.scenario: Ongoing action returns Object.freeze({onMove, onEnd}); a param tuning wraps it; isEmptyOngoingHandle throws on the first method read
defects.cause: Proxy substitutes non-configurable, non-writable properties

defects.claim: Held-key preview and release check enabled without the view id and with a made-up world point, unlike the dispatcher's admission
defects.scenario: Hold bound in view `detail` with enabled true only for `detail`; dispatcher admits it, but showPreview/checkEnabled get no view, so nothing previews and release does nothing
defects.cause: routing facts not carried into gate calls

defects.claim: After an id change, drive sends the new action's input to the previous action's open control
defects.scenario: Open A with input; switch the id to B and call edit.input from a layout effect; A gets B's params and commits, and B never opens
defects.cause: effect ordering versus the latest-id ref

defects.claim: begin admits the child's action, but an inherited parent dispatcher starts the parent's implementation without its gate
defects.scenario: A nested InputScope with no dispatcher registers a different ongoing action at the same id; begin through the child starts the parent's action with the child's deps
defects.cause: dispatcher looks the id up again instead of using the admitted descriptor

defects.claim: Adjusting an immediate last operation replays raw given params, so the current tuning changes params the form doesn't show
defects.scenario: Thunk tuning gives axis x; trigger; change the thunk to y; adjust distance in the panel; the replay uses axis y
defects.cause: immediate path doesn't capture resolved params

defects.claim: A mixed modifier/letter held-key alias lets Ctrl/Cmd+letter start the offhand tool and blocks the browser chord
defects.scenario: buildToolOffhandBindings([{toolId:'hand', key:['Shift','k']}]); Cmd+K starts the hand tool and prevents the browser default
defects.cause: mods relaxation applied spec-wide

defects.claim: Shortcut lookup evaluates params thunks for bindings that have no displayable shortcut, and one can throw
defects.scenario: A variant with a keyboard binding and a pointer binding whose thunk needs pointer state; actionItemShortcuts runs the thunk early and it throws
defects.cause: params evaluated before the shortcut filter

defects.claim: A tuning's params never reach ctx.params of a UI-driven ongoing action begun without params
defects.scenario: `registry.tune('opacity.set', { params: { step: 0.1 } })`, then a control calls `begin('opacity.set')` with no params (or `useOngoingAction(...).input` before any value). The dispatcher starts the invoker with `uiInvocationCtx(deps, undefined)` (`dispatcher/uiOngoing.ts:92`); `wrapInvoker` lays the tuning only when `ctx.params` is set (`ctx.params ? { ...ctx, params: base(ctx.params) } : ctx`), so the action reading `ctx.params` — where the `InvocationCtx.params` doc says UI-driven actions get theirs — sees no tuned params on start, then sees them on the first `update` that carries params. The `ActionTuning.params` doc promises "params every invocation starts from". The same guard on `onMove` drops them for an update with no params.
defects.cause: tuning laid only over present params

defects.claim: trigger reports true ("it ran") when the action's run threw
defects.scenario: `run` throws partway (say a missing dep in prod). The catch logs the error and falls through to `return true`. The contract in `registry.ts` says `trigger` returns whether it ran one, and lists every other failure as `false`. A palette or menu caller that treats `true` as "done" (closing, toasting success) reports success for a failed command. It should return `false` from the catch.
defects.cause: catch falls through to the success return

defects.claim: A hold made by holdPreview keeps the label of the descriptor it was made from, not the live one it follows
defects.scenario: `holdPreview(defaultAction)` is registered, and a consumer later registers a replacement under `action.id` with another label. `holdingLive` replaces the gates and invoker with the live action's but keeps `rest.label` from the hold, which is the original's label. The doc says the hold "follows whatever that registry resolves for `action.id`: its replacement". A keymap editor or a shortcut list showing the hold names the replaced action.
defects.cause: label copied once at construction, not taken from the live action

defects.claim: Tuned, session and binding params merge shallowly, so a nested param group loses leaves
defects.scenario: an action's `params` form has a group, e.g. `fill.color` and `fill.opacity`. After a last-operation adjust, the session tuning holds the nested `{ fill: { color, opacity } }` (`remember` → `nestPrefValues`). A binding or `trigger` then passes `{ fill: { color: 'red' } }`, and `tunedParams` does `{ ...out, ...given }`, which replaces the whole `fill` object, so `fill.opacity` from the session or a tuning is dropped and the run uses the action's default. `lastOperation.withValues` sets values by leaf path, so the store does treat params as nested; the layering that feeds `run`, `paramsOf` and `invokedParams` does not.
defects.cause: shallow spread over nested param groups

defects.claim: holdPreview of a legacy-bag action with an `eligible` rule passes only `ruleCtx`, losing every other dep
defects.scenario: an action with no `requires` (so `depsFor` hands it the legacy fixed bag: selection, scene, history, view, activeTool, booleansAdapter) but with an `eligible` rule is wrapped by `holdPreview`. `holding` gives the hold `requires: [...(action.requires ?? []), 'ruleCtx']` = `['ruleCtx']`, so the hold's deps are built by `createActionDeps` from that list alone. On the press, `showPreview` calls `action.enabled` / `action.preview` with that bag; in dev the deps Proxy throws on `deps.selection` (enabled reads as `predicate-threw`, preview logs and shows nothing), in prod they read `undefined`. On release `invoker.run(ctx.deps, now)` runs without `scene`/`selection`. Expected: the hold gets the deps the action itself would get — the legacy bag plus `ruleCtx`, or the action's gates and run read through the action's own deps.
defects.cause: `requires` added where the action declared none flips it from the legacy bag to declared deps

defects.claim: adjust stores session params for an action whose tuning `keep`s them, so they surface once that tuning is removed
defects.scenario: a tool's options tuning with `keep` is live for action X; the user changes a value in the last-operation panel. `adjust` calls `held.keep(...)` (correct) and also `this.remember(id, values)` unconditionally. `tuningsOf` hides the session tuning only while a `keep` tuning is present; after a tool switch releases that tuning, the stale session params come back and are laid over every `under` tuning (tool defaults) for the rest of the session. docs/unruled.md (round fourteen) rules that such an action "stores no session params". Expected: skip `remember` when a tuning of `id` keeps the params.
defects.cause: session write not gated on a keeping tuning

defects.claim: A yoke member mounted under another `<ActionsProvider>` takes that provider's menu host instead of its yoke tree's
defects.scenario: `useYoke()` is called under ActionsProvider P1; a canvas `<InputScope yoke={yoke}>` sits elsewhere, under ActionsProvider P2 (the `Yoke` doc says members "can sit anywhere in the tree"). Its actions/deps/tool nodes hang on P1's tree, but `Provide` takes `useContext(MenuHostContext)`, which is P2's, before falling back to `nodes.actions.menuHost()`. Context menus and menu rows inside that canvas list and trigger P2's actions against P2's active scope, never the canvas's own. Expected: use the menu host of the tree the nodes belong to (`nodes.actions.menuHost()`), which already returns the root's shared host.
defects.cause: menu host chosen by React location rather than by the node's tree
